transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-01
Start: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Kim (Redwood AE), Omar Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Cobalt Lead Data Engineer), Evan Li (Cobalt ML Engineer), Sarah Morales (Cobalt Security), Tom Baxter (Cobalt Product)

Summary (auto): quick check of onboarding tasks, confirmation of VPC peering steps, KMS access, sample data readiness, and scheduling of perf benchmark.

--- Transcript (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect) ---
[00:00:05] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is our usual weekly POC sync for Cobalt Finance, unit of Redwood. Quick roll call - Omar from my side, and we have Priya, Evan, Sarah, Tom.
[00:00:18] Priya: Hi, yep, on my side.
[00:00:20] Evan: Morning.
[00:00:22] Sarah: Hi all.
[00:00:25] Omar: Hi team.
[00:00:30] Lena: Cool. Agenda - onboarding status, env readiness, any blockers, then next steps and scheduling the performance benchmark. Omar, want to take the onboarding checklist?
[00:00:40] Omar: Sure. So last week we asked for VPC peering, a test AWS account and a KMS key. Priya, do you have updates on the peering?
[00:00:50] Priya: Uh, yes. We started but hit a couple issues - the network team required an explicit route table update and our VPC CIDR was overlapping with another internal VPC, so we've been reassigning subnets. Should be resolved by EOD tomorrow though.
[00:01:05] Lena: Okay great, that aligns. Once peering is in place we can do a quick smoke test. Omar, you mentioned a peering checklist?
[00:01:12] Omar: Yeah I have a checklist and sample Terraform script. I'll drop that in the shared folder after the call. It covers security group rules, route tables, IAM roles for the Redwood service account, and the NAT/egress expectations.
[00:01:25] Priya: Perfect. For IAM, we prefer to do least privilege - can you give exact permissions needed for the service account?
[00:01:32] Omar: Absolutely, I'll include a minimal policy. It mostly needs S3 read for the sample data bucket, CloudWatch put logs, and ability to assume a role in the customer's account.
[00:01:45] Tom: Quick question - do we need full access to KMS or just encrypt/decrypt?
[00:01:50] Sarah: From security, we want customer-managed CMK and we only allow decrypt/encrypt. No admin on customer side. We'll provide a key policy that allows Redwood's service principal.
[00:02:02] Lena: Good. Omar, can you add the KMS key policy example to the doc?
[00:02:07] Omar: Yup, will add that.
[00:02:10] Evan: On our side I spun up a small test cluster for inference, but I haven't piped it into Redwood because of the peering gap. I did run some local emulation and saw token latencies in the 150-220ms range for short prompts on our infra. We want to compare against Redwood hosted baseline.
[00:02:27] Omar: Perfect, that's what the benchmark next week should capture. We also want to test with dynamic batching and KV cache enabled. Just a heads up, our runtime selects different kernels based on sequence length so we should give a mix of short and medium sequences.
[00:02:42] Priya: What are the sequence lengths we should include? Typical is 32, 128, 512 tokens for us.
[00:02:49] Omar: Yep, include 32 and 128 for low-latency, and 512 for throughput. Also include a few long-context prompts if you have them.
[00:02:57] Lena: On pricing - Evan you asked about dedicated vs hosted. Any updates from procurement?
[00:03:04] Evan: Procurement is ok to start with hosted for the pilot due to time to value, but we want to evaluate Dedicated for phase 2 if latency and throughput are good. Cost is the main trade-off.
[00:03:14] Lena: Makes sense. We'll put both options in the PoC pricing - hosted hourly estimate and a dedicated reserved estimate. I'll send SOW and numbers after this call.
[00:03:23] Priya: Sarah also flagged audit logs - we need audit trails and retention controls for the PoC.
[00:03:29] Sarah: Right, SOC2 compliance is a must. We also need to ensure logs don't contain raw PII. Can Redwood redact or mask tokens before logs?
[00:03:38] Omar: We have configurable logging at the route level - you can disable token-level logging, or we can do structured logging that strips embeddings and redacts certain fields. I'll include recommended settings.
[00:03:49] Lena: We'll also share our SOC2 + KMS docs.
[00:03:53] Sarah: Please.
[00:03:55] [00:04:05] Priya: About data - we'll provide a PII-masked subset this week. We need to confirm how to upload - S3 bucket or direct upload?
[00:04:12] Omar: S3 is easiest. We'll give a bucket policy and a pre-signed URL approach in the doc. For the benchmark we recommend sample sizes of ~10k short prompts and 2k medium prompts.
[00:04:24] Evan: One more thing - are there any known model variants that Redwood recommends for finance workloads? We've seen hallucinations in some LLMs with domain-specific prompts.
[00:04:34] Omar: We onboarded a curated model that balances hallucination mitigations and latency; I'll include the model name and quantization profile. For sensitive tasks we typically suggest smaller context windows and stronger prompt templates plus a reranker.
[00:04:48] Tom: Nice. Can you share any published benchmarks?
[00:04:51] Omar: Yes - I'll attach the per-model latency/cost sheet. Note that numbers vary by GPU type and sequence length.
[00:04:59] Priya: Regarding the peering steps, is there any downtime to expect?
[00:05:04] Omar: No, peering itself doesn't cause downtime; just ensure route tables are updated. If subnets need to be re-assigned we recommend a maintenance window but it's usually seamless.
[00:05:15] [00:05:30] Sarah: On KMS - we need to confirm that Redwood supports customer-managed keys in the region we use (eu-west-1).
[00:05:36] Lena: Yes we do, but I'm going to confirm region specifics in the security doc link.
[00:05:41] Omar: Also note for private deployment there's an option for an on-prem package if you need air-gapped later. That's a longer lead time but possible.
[00:05:52] Evan: For now we prefer hosted + VPC peering. If the latency is within our SLO we can evaluate Dedicated in Q3.
[00:06:01] Lena: Sounds good. Let's talk timeline - peering expected by 2026-04-02 per Priya, test data by 2026-04-05, then we aim to run benchmarks on 2026-04-08. Any conflicts?
[00:06:12] Priya: That timeline works for us.
[00:06:14] Tom: Works for product.
[00:06:16] Sarah: Works for security as long as we get the KMS key policy by 2026-04-06.
[00:06:22] Lena: Great. Next, a few clarifications on telemetry - Evan, you said you saw 150-220ms locally. That's helpful, but our hosted baseline may be sub-100ms for short prompts depending on region. We'll measure both cold and warmed cache.
[00:06:36] Evan: Good to know.
[00:06:38] Omar: During the benchmark we'll run cold starts and steady-state runs to show both tail-latency and p50/p95. We'll also run a test with batching to show cost improvements.
[00:06:48] [00:07:05] Priya: On security scans - are there automated scans Redwood runs on code or images? We need to align with our security pipeline.
[00:07:14] Omar: For hosted we run vulnerability scanning on images and have process-level isolation; for dedicated we can integrate with your scanner during image build. I'll include details.
[00:07:25] Sarah: Please include CVE scan cadence and evidence of remediation.
[00:07:30] Omar: Noted.
[00:07:33] Lena: Okay let's recap action items quickly. Omar will send the peering checklist + Terraform + KMS policy example. Lena will send PoC pricing and SOW. Priya/Evan will provision test account and sample data. Sarah will provide KMS policy contact. We'll plan the benchmark for 2026-04-08.
[00:07:50] Priya: Sounds good.
[00:07:53] Evan: Good.
[00:07:55] [00:08:10] Tom: One last Q - in case of capacity constraints, does Redwood have automated fallback to smaller models or other regions?
[00:08:20] Omar: Yes, we have routing policies to fallback to compatible model variants or other regions; we'll discuss during the perf run if you want to see an example.
[00:08:29] Lena: I'll set up a follow-up demo if needed.
[00:08:33] [00:08:45] Sarah: Ok, thanks everyone.
[00:08:48] Lena: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the docs and next steps.
[00:08:52] [00:09:00] <<call ended - remaining ~36 minutes were not recorded due to calendar wrap, transcript truncated>>

Notes: transcription contains typical Fireflies OCR-like artifacts (speaker chops, minor mis-hearings). Links referenced: /shared/poc/peering-checklist (will be uploaded), SOC2 & KMS doc link (to be shared), per-model latency/cost spreadsheet (attached by Omar).
